name: SEVEN CUTS: The Knife-Dealer's Dice Game
description: A fast, brutal dice game for 2–6 players using seven asymmetric dice — each carved with faction symbols rather than numbers — in which players bid Quanta against a rotating 'Dealer' who controls the cut sequence, a layered reveal mechanic that rewards bluffing and punishes hesitation. Smart-ink score tiles shift to track running debt in real time, turning red when a player's loss crosses a threshold set by the table. Originally designed by a Tier 2 dice carver named Priya Oduya-Magnusson who sold hand-carved sets from a market stall, Seven Cuts spread through Shelf gambling dens within eighteen months of its 2218 introduction.
story_hooks: Priya Oduya-Magnusson's original prototype dice are rumored to be loaded in a mathematically precise way that gives the Dealer a 4% edge — and she has never denied it.
A Tier 4 game theorist arrives on the Shelf claiming to have solved Seven Cuts optimal strategy; the locals are skeptical, but someone is paying her very well to be there.
The faction symbols on the dice correspond to real corponation insignia — and a symbol that appeared on the original 2218 set belongs to a corponation that officially ceased to exist in 2211.
